narrative:
The model estimates an 82% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your total years of professional experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and whether you have received other job offers. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter careers (1–5 years is most common among stayers), your mid-level experience aligns more with people who eventually move on. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in this organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction. This tenure is actually the most frequent range among those expected to stay, but in your specific combination of factors it still signaled higher turnover risk. Finally, the fact that you have received other job opportunities outside the company was a significant driver toward leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay do not report receiving such offers.

Taken together, these elements created a profile the model associates with departure. The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths or addressing the external opportunities you are seeing. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term career goals.
